name: routing
rubric: Score each prompt 0 to 2 on three axes: right pattern (or correctly says no pattern fits), right caveat, right link. A caveat that is only available by fetching the page earns at most 1.

items.prompt: When a later step fails I need to undo the earlier ones: release the hold, refund the card. How do I do that in a workflow?
items.key_caveat: Register each compensation as soon as its step is attempted, run them in reverse order, and make compensations idempotent and retryable (they can also fail). Use Non-Retryable Errors for business failures that should trigger compensation instead of retrying.

items.prompt: Our long-running workflow is getting history size warnings after a few months of events. What do we do?
items.key_caveat: Use the SDK's continue-as-new-suggested check rather than a hand-picked count; let Signal and Update handlers finish before continuing, and carry forward only the state you need. Warning at 10,240 Events / 10 MB, hard stop at 51,200 / 50 MB.

items.prompt: Events for an order come off our message bus. The workflow for that order may not exist yet. Start it if it is missing, otherwise just deliver the event.
items.key_caveat: Use a deterministic business key as the Workflow ID. Temporal has no native Kafka/SQS consumer: the existing consumer calls Signal-with-Start. Keep the per-execution Signal rate low (about 5 per second sustained).

items.prompt: The caller needs a synchronous answer: validate the request, change the workflow's state and return a result, and reject bad input before it is recorded.
items.key_caveat: Use an Update validator to reject before anything is written to history. Limits: 10 in-flight Updates and 2,000 total Updates per execution; Updates are slower than Signals.

items.prompt: A reviewer has to approve before we continue. If nobody approves within 48 hours, escalate to their manager.
items.key_caveat: Wait on the approval with a durable timer (await condition with timeout); the timer survives restarts and deploys. Use an Update instead of a Signal if the approver's UI needs confirmation or validation. If the deadline can move, add Updatable Timer.

items.prompt: The partner API allows 50 calls per second in total across all of our workers. How do we stay under it?
items.key_caveat: Put the throttled Activity on its own Task Queue with a server-enforced dispatch cap: Worker option maxTaskQueueActivitiesPerSecond, or 'temporal task-queue config set --queue-rps-limit', which overrides the Worker option and decouples it from deploys. Retries count against the cap; set it a little under the partner limit because of per-partition bursts.

items.prompt: One big tenant floods the shared queue and everyone else's work sits behind it.
items.key_caveat: Fairness (GA) with a fairness key per tenant and optional weights; optional per-key rate limit. It is not hard isolation; use separate Task Queues or Namespaces for that. Priority is a different tool (strict ordering, not sharing).

items.prompt: We have to process about 2 million records from a file without blowing up the workflow history.
items.key_caveat: Page through the data and Continue-As-New between pages; combine with Sliding Window or Fan-Out with Child Workflows for parallelism. Keep pending Activities or Children per execution under 2,000 (aim for 500 or fewer).

items.prompt: Ask three quote providers at once, use whichever answers first, and stop the other two.
items.key_caveat: Cancel the losers with a cancellation scope; a running Activity only sees the cancel on its next Heartbeat, so the provider calls need heartbeats (and idempotent side effects).

items.prompt: The payment API returns 429 with a Retry-After header. We want to wait exactly that long before the next try.
items.key_caveat: Throw an ApplicationFailure with nextRetryDelay set from the header; it overrides only that interval, and the Retry Policy's maximum attempts and Schedule-To-Close still apply.

items.prompt: Validation failures keep retrying forever even though they will never succeed.
items.key_caveat: Mark the error type non-retryable (in the Retry Policy or on the thrown ApplicationFailure) so the Workflow fails fast and can compensate or report.

items.prompt: Partner outages can last hours. We want quick retries at first, then slow retries for as long as it takes, and on-call should know when it is stuck.
items.key_caveat: Fast phase then slow unlimited phase so the Workflow outlasts the outage; emit a metric past an attempt threshold for alerting. Operators can also Pause the Activity during a known outage (Activity Operations, Public Preview).

items.prompt: A file has to be processed on the same host that downloaded it, then cleaned up there.
items.key_caveat: Return a host-specific Task Queue name from the first Activity and route the rest there; if that host dies, the Workflow must retry from the download step on another host.

items.prompt: Several services send pieces of data for the same case over a few minutes. Collect them and process them together once things go quiet.
items.key_caveat: Deduplicate by event ID, reset an inactivity timer on each Signal, start with Signal-with-Start; per-execution Signal rate about 5 per second sustained and 10,000 per run (Continue-As-New if long-lived).

items.prompt: Which patterns fit a travel booking platform? We hold the fare, charge the card, issue the ticket; the booking can change for weeks after; and the API must confirm in a couple of seconds.

expected.non_pattern: durable timer for the ticketing deadline; Workflow ID as booking key

items.key_caveat: Early Return uses Update-with-Start; a durable timer races ticketing against the hold deadline; Workflow ID as the booking key with ID conflict policy Use Existing for duplicate submits; Continue-As-New for long-lived bookings.

items.prompt: Money transfer service: withdraw, deposit, never double-move money, and transfers over a threshold need a manual approval.

expected.non_pattern: idempotency keys; Workflow ID as transfer reference

items.key_caveat: Activities are at-least-once: pass one idempotency key (deterministic, made in the Workflow or by the caller) to withdraw and deposit; Workflow ID as the transfer reference blocks duplicate starts; compensation on deposit failure.

items.prompt: We are building an AI agent platform: a long LLM loop calling tools, human approval before risky tools, and the UI should stream tokens as they come.

expected.non_pattern: Workflow as agent loop with LLM and tool calls as Activities; Workflow Streams for token streaming; External Storage for large context; SDK AI integrations

items.key_caveat: LLM and tool calls must be Activities (non-deterministic). Token streaming uses Workflow Streams (experimental), not Queries or a Signal per token. Continue-As-New for long conversations; keep conversation payloads small or offload them.

items.prompt: Nightly ETL over tens of millions of rows. We need retries, and we can't hammer the source database.

expected.non_pattern: Schedules to trigger it nightly

items.key_caveat: Schedules (a feature, not a catalog pattern) start the run; Batch Iterator plus Sliding Window bound concurrency; a Task Queue rate limit protects the database. Pass row IDs or page cursors, not row data (2 MB payload limit).

items.prompt: Multi-tenant SaaS that syncs each tenant's CRM. Every tenant has its own API credentials and rate limit, and one tenant must not slow down the rest.
items.key_caveat: One shared Activity Task Queue per CRM with a fairness key per tenant credential and a per-fairness-key rate limit (scaled by weight). Partitions reduce per-key accuracy at low limits; use separate queues for hard isolation.

items.prompt: Device lifecycle management: each device is provisioned, gets config pushes and health checks, and is retired years later.
items.key_caveat: One Workflow per device with Signals or Updates for commands; Continue-As-New regularly; keep per-device message rate low; plan Worker Versioning for code changes across long-lived runs.

items.prompt: Order fulfillment where the carrier calls our webhook days later with delivery status.
items.key_caveat: Inbound webhook becomes a Signal (or Signal-with-Start) keyed by order ID, or the Activity completes asynchronously via task token; set a timer for the carrier never calling back.

items.prompt: Checkout API has a tight latency budget. The first response must come back fast while the rest of the order processing continues.
items.key_caveat: Update-with-Start returns the first result; Local Activities in phase 1 skip server round trips (at-least-once, short and idempotent only); Eager Workflow Start needs the starter and Worker co-located. Measure before adding all three.

items.prompt: We need the charge to happen exactly once. Can Temporal guarantee exactly-once execution if we set retries to one attempt?

expected.non_pattern: No pattern gives exactly-once side effects. Activities are at-least-once; use idempotency keys (Workflow Run ID + Activity ID, or a business key) enforced by the payment service, plus Workflow ID dedupe for starts.
must_not: fixed-count-retries as the answer to exactly-once
saga-pattern as the answer to exactly-once

items.key_caveat: maxAttempts=1 gives at-most-once and still does not prevent a duplicate if a Worker crashes after the side effect but before reporting. Workflow code is effectively-once; Activities are not.

items.prompt: We handle about 50k events per second; each one is a single outbound call that needs retries and a record. Should each event be its own workflow?

expected.non_pattern: Standalone Activities (GA, Temporal's job queue): one durable, retryable, addressable Activity per event without a Workflow. Use a Workflow only when there are multiple dependent steps, waits or state.

items.key_caveat: Activity ID as the dedupe key with a conflict policy; Activity code still idempotent. At this rate, plan Namespace capacity with the account team. Do not funnel the events into one Workflow.

items.prompt: To protect a downstream API we built a semaphore workflow: every workflow signals it to ask for a slot and waits for a reply signal. It falls behind under load. How do we scale it?

expected.non_pattern: Server-side Task Queue rate limit (queue-rps-limit) or per-fairness-key limits replace the semaphore Workflow
must_not: a sharded mutex Workflow as the primary answer

items.key_caveat: A single coordinating Workflow is capped by per-execution Signal throughput (about 5 per second sustained). Use the server-enforced Task Queue rate limit; for concurrency (not rate) caps, size Worker slots.

items.prompt: The approval request should expire after three days, but an approver can extend the deadline while it is still open.
items.key_caveat: Plain Approval with a fixed timeout misses the moving deadline: the extend action is a Signal or Update that resets the timer. Use an Update validator to reject approvals or extensions after expiry.

items.prompt: Our chat assistant workflow lives for weeks with thousands of turns, and every Activity call passes the full conversation history.

expected.non_pattern: External Storage (claim check, Public Preview) or store the transcript outside and pass a reference
must_not: entity-workflow alone with no history or payload caveat

items.key_caveat: Two limits: history length (Continue-As-New, carry a summary) and payload size (2 MB per payload; full history per call bloats Event History fast). If each turn is an Update, the 2,000 total Updates per run also forces Continue-As-New.

items.prompt: Our parent workflow starts 10,000 child workflows at once, one per account. It works in test but fails in production.
items.key_caveat: 2,000 pending Child Workflows per execution is a hard limit (aim for 500 or fewer); Sliding Window caps in-flight children and Continue-As-New keeps the parent's history bounded. Batch Iterator or MapReduce Tree for larger sets.

items.prompt: Users double-click submit. The second request should attach to the booking that is already running instead of starting another one.

expected.non_pattern: Workflow ID as the business key with Workflow ID Conflict Policy USE_EXISTING (default FAIL returns already-started); Update-with-Start if the caller needs a result
must_not: signal-with-start as the primary answer when no message is being sent

items.key_caveat: Conflict policy covers a running Workflow; Reuse Policy covers a closed one. Starts to the same ID too fast hit ID-reuse rate limits.

items.prompt: Local Activities are faster, so can we make all our Activities local, including the 30-second calls to the core banking system?

expected.non_pattern: Keep long or remote calls as regular Activities

items.key_caveat: Local Activities fit short (a few seconds), idempotent calls on a latency path. They run inside the Workflow Task, re-run if the Worker crashes before the task completes, get no Task Queue rate limiting or Activity Operations, and long ones need Workflow Task heartbeating.

items.prompt: Run the reconciliation every night at 2 a.m., and skip a run if yesterday's is still going.

expected.non_pattern: Schedules with an overlap policy (Skip is the default)
must_not: a Workflow that loops with a 24-hour sleep

items.key_caveat: Delayed Start is one-time; recurring work is a Schedule (pause, backfill, overlap policy built in).

items.prompt: Another team in a different namespace needs to call our payment workflow with a typed contract, without sharing our code or getting write access to our namespace.

expected.non_pattern: Nexus (Nexus Services and Operations through a Nexus Endpoint)

items.key_caveat: Release stage varies by SDK (GA in Go, Java, Python; Public Preview in TypeScript and .NET as of the 2026 announcements); 30 in-flight Nexus Operations per caller Workflow.

items.prompt: Every time we deploy new workflow code, running workflows fail with non-determinism errors. How do we ship changes safely?

expected.non_pattern: Worker Versioning (GA) with pinned or auto-upgrade behavior; patching APIs for in-place changes; replay tests in CI

items.key_caveat: Pinned Workflows finish on the version that started them; long-lived ones move with Continue-As-New or auto-upgrade plus patches. Run replay tests against production histories before deploy.

items.prompt: Support needs to find every booking stuck at the payment step for a given customer.

expected.non_pattern: Custom Search Attributes (for example customer ID and step) plus List Filter queries in the UI or CLI
must_not: a Query fan-out to every Workflow

items.key_caveat: Register attributes on the Namespace and upsert them as the step changes; Visibility is eventually consistent and rate limited, so it is not a transactional store.

items.prompt: We need in-memory processing of market ticks at about a million events per second with sub-millisecond latency. Is Temporal the right tool?

expected.non_pattern: Temporal is not the right fit for the hot path; use a stream processor and use Temporal for the durable processes around it (onboarding, settlement, remediation)
must_not: any catalog pattern as the hot-path answer

items.key_caveat: Every Workflow step is a durable write; per-execution throughput is a few events per second. Say so instead of forcing a pattern.

items.prompt: We keep one long-lived entity workflow per device as the source of truth. Other services query it many times a second and do compare-and-swap through Updates. Is that a good design?

expected.non_pattern: Don't: a Workflow is not a high-rate datastore or per-record state store. Keep record state in a database; use Workflows for bounded processes that act on it (provision, replace, retire).

items.key_caveat: 10 in-flight Updates per execution (excess rejected with resource exhausted), Signals about 5 per second, Queries need a Worker and replay, Continue-As-New across hundreds of millions of runs and every Worker version is costly and handler-drain mistakes are easy.

items.prompt: We want one global counter workflow that every service signals to increment usage.

expected.non_pattern: Don't: single-execution hot spot. Use a database counter, or shard across many Workflows and aggregate on a schedule.

items.key_caveat: Per-execution Signal guidance is about 5 per second sustained; above that you get BUSY_WORKFLOW and lock contention, and 10,000 Signals per run.

items.prompt: Can we call the LLM and our REST APIs directly from workflow code? Wrapping everything in Activities feels like boilerplate.

expected.non_pattern: Don't: Workflow code must be deterministic. Network calls, LLM calls, randomness and clocks go in Activities (or SDK-provided deterministic APIs).
must_not: local-activities as a way to skip Activities

items.key_caveat: Direct I/O in Workflow code breaks replay. SDK AI integrations already wrap model calls as Activities; Activity Dependency Injection keeps clients out of Workflow code.

items.prompt: We pass the whole 20 MB document as the workflow input and hand it from Activity to Activity.

expected.non_pattern: Don't: 2 MB per payload limit. Store the blob externally and pass a reference (claim check), or use External Storage (Public Preview).

items.key_caveat: Even under 2 MB, large payloads accumulate in Event History and slow Workflow Tasks; the limit is fixed at 2 MB on Temporal Cloud.

items.prompt: Our workflow polls a status API every second in a while loop with a one-second sleep, forever.

expected.non_pattern: Don't poll at high frequency from Workflow code: each iteration adds Events.

items.key_caveat: Frequent polling belongs inside one heartbeating Activity; infrequent polling uses the Activity Retry Policy as the loop; any Workflow-level loop needs Continue-As-New. Prefer a callback or Signal if the system can push.
